Functional validation of OsRPM1 using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout (KO) and overexpression (OX) lines confirmed its positive role in blast resistance, where KO mutants exhibited increased lesion length and higher pathogen accumulation. In contrast, OX lines showed enhanced resistance and improved photosynthetic performance and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) accumulation. These findings provide a comprehensive resource of candidate genes and regulatory modules for functional validation and molecular breeding, offering a robust foundation for developing rice cultivars with broad-spectrum and durable blast resistance.

title: LncRNA TRHDE-AS1 functions as a tumor suppressor via the miR-22-5p/DLG3 axis to regulate malignant phenotypes and predict prognosis in glioma.
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) represent a significant avenue for investigating tumor molecular mechanisms and identifying potential therapeutic targets. It was aimed to explore the expression and prognostic significance of lncRNA TRHDE-AS1 in glioma, and clarify its ceRNA-mediated regulation of miR-22-5p/DLG3 axis in promoting glioma progression in vitro. Using the TCGA database and clinical glioma tissue samples (n = 150), qRT-PCR was employed to detect the expression of TRHDE-AS1. Its prognostic value was assessed through Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression analysis. The targeting interaction between TRHDE-AS1, miR-22-5p and DLG3 was confirmed by luciferase reporter assay and RNA Immunoprecipitation (RIP) experiments. Using CCK-8 and Transwell assays, the impact of TRHDE-AS1 on glioma cells' malignant phenotypes was evaluated. To assess the influence on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), the protein levels of N-cadherin, Snail, and MMP-2 were measured via Western blot. Low expression of TRHDE-AS1 in glioma tissues correlated with patients' malignant features, consistent with findings from the TCGA database. It was independently related to reduced overall survival. Upon TRHDE-AS1 upregulation, miR-22-5p levels significantly decreased while downstream target DLG3 expression increased in both U251 and LN229 cells. The proliferation, invasive metastatic ability and EMT of both cells were significantly reduced, which was offset by miR-22-5p overexpression. TRHDE-AS1/miR-22-5p mediated cellular phenotype alterations were restored by DLG3 again in both U251 and LN229 cells. Downregulation of TRHDE-AS1 was closely related to glioma patients' poor prognosis. It may regulate miR-22-5p/DLG3 axis through the ceRNA mechanism to promote the malignant activity of glioma cells.

title: ZNF460-SNRPB-RDM1 splicing axis promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression through regulation of DNA damage repair.
abstract: Small nuclear ribonucleoprotein polypeptide B (SNRPB) is one of the core proteins of the spliceosome. Although its role in spliceosome assembly has been well - established, its carcinogenic potential has just begun to be revealed. We found that its expression is significantly increased in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and is associated with a poor prognosis. Mechanistically, this study reveals a carcinogenic axis centered around abnormal RNA splicing: the ZNF460-SNRPB-RDM1 axis. The upstream transcription factor ZNF460 transcriptionally activates SNRPB through a predicted ZNF460-responsive element in the SNRPB promoter, leading to the abnormally high expression of the core spliceosome protein SNRPB in ccRCC. Excessive SNRPB interferes with the precise splicing of RDM1 pre-mRNA, resulting in the dysregulated expression of functional RDM1 protein. As a protein implicated in DNA damage repair and homologous recombination-associated processes, changes in the expression level of RDM1 alter the sensitivity of ccRCC cells to the PARP inhibitor olaparib. Therefore, this axis is not only a newly discovered driver of ccRCC invasiveness and drug resistance but may also be a new therapeutic target.

title: [Mechanism of endothelial cell-derived S100A11 in promoting radiation-induced cardiac fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice].
abstract: Objective: To investigate the role and mechanism of cardiac endothelial cell-derived S100A11 in promoting radiotherapy-induced cardiac fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice. Methods: Eight 6-week-old female C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into a control group (n=4) and a radiotherapy group (n=4) using a random number table. The control group received no intervention, while the radiotherapy group received a single high-dose irradiation of 16 Gy to the left thorax to establish a mouse model of cardiac injury. At 12 weeks after radiotherapy, echocardiography was performed to measure left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular fractional shortening (LVFS), and left ventricular internal dimension at end-systole (LVIDs). Western blotting was used to detect the expression of collagen type Ⅰ (COL Ⅰ) and alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) in mouse cardiac tissue. The mouse cardiac endothelial cell line MCEC were divided into a control group and a radiotherapy group (medium was replaced after endothelial cell adherence, followed by radiotherapy and continued culture for 24 h before sample collection). The supernatants from the control and radiotherapy endothelial cell groups were mixed with complete medium at a 1∶1 ratio and used to culture primary cardiac fibroblasts extracted from C57BL/6 mouse cardiac tissue. These fibroblasts were divided into a control group and a treatment group. Western blotting was used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression and a scratch assay was used to assess cell migration ability. Endothelial cells were divided into a control group and a radiotherapy group. Western blotting, quantitative real-time PCR, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were used to detect the expression and secretion of S100 calcium-binding protein A11 (S100A11) in endothelial cells. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was used to knock down S100A11 gene expression in endothelial cells. Two siRNAs targeting S100A11 and a siRNA negative control group were separately transfected into endothelial cells. Western blotting was used to verify whether S100A11 expression in endothelial cells was successfully knocked down. The S100A11-knockdown endothelial cells were then subjected to radiotherapy and divided into a control group, siRNA-1 group, and siRNA-2 group. The sample collection method and the method for co-culturing primary fibroblasts were the same as described above, with groups designated as control, siRNA-1, and siRNA-2. Western blotting was used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression. Primary fibroblasts were treated with recombinant S100A11 protein (100 ng/ml) for 24 h, and Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA expression. Transcriptome sequencing was used to detect gene expression changes in primary fibroblasts treated with recombinant S100A11 protein for 24 h. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was used to knock down integrin subunit beta-like 1 (ITGBL1) gene expression in primary fibroblasts. Two siRNAs targeting ITGBL1 (siRNA-1 and siRNA-2) (i.e., the siRNA group) and a siRNA negative control (si-NC) group were separately transfected into primary fibroblasts. Western blotting was used to verify knockdown of ITGBL1 expression in primary fibroblasts. Primary fibroblasts with ITGBL1 knockdown were cultured with recombinant S100A11 protein for 24 h, and Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to detect COLⅠ and α-SMA protein expression. Results: Compared with the control group, echocardiography showed that LVEF and LVFS were lower in the radiotherapy group (both P<0.001), and COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression levels in cardiac tissue were higher in the radiotherapy group (both P<0.001). Perivascular fibrotic tissue in the hearts of irradiated mice was increased than that of the control group (all P<0.05). The mRNA, protein, and supernatant protein expression of S100A11 in endothelial cells were higher in the radiotherapy group than in the control group (all P<0.001). The supernatant from radiotherapy-treated endothelial cells increased and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts compared with the control group (all P<0.05). In S100A11-knockdown endothelial cells subjected to radiotherapy, COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts in the siRNA groups were lower than in the control group (all P<0.05). Recombinant S100A11 protein increased COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts compared with the control group (all P<0.05). Transcriptome sequencing indicated that ITGBL1 gene expression levels were higher in primary fibroblasts treated with recombinant S100A11 protein than in the control group. After ITGBL1 knockdown, S100A11 promoted COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts were lower than in the control group (P<0.05). Conclusions: After radiotherapy, S100A11 expression and secretion are increased in cardiac endothelial cells. This effect can further activate cardiac fibroblasts in C57BL/6 mice and promote the development and progression of cardiac fibrosis.

title: High-Gain Bacterial RNA Imaging via High-Density Protein Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization.
abstract: Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is important for bacterial genotypic analysis; however, the limited number of labels per probe results in insufficient signal gain, compromising the detection of low-abundance RNAs. Here, we present high-density protein FISH (HD-FISH) for high-gain bacterial RNA imaging. Instead of fluorophore-modified probes, this method employs a fluorescently tagged, catalytically inactive ribonuclease H1 for multi-site labeling of target RNAs. Compared to traditional FISH and hybridization chain reaction-based FISH, HD-FISH suppresses background noise while enhancing positive signals, achieving 7.43-fold and 1.89-fold increases in signal gain, respectively, thereby enabling high-gain imaging. We showed that HD-FISH can precisely quantify quinolone-resistant Salmonella enterica strains within complex microbial communities, with a recovery rate of 97.78-131.40%, and allows us to detect and identify quinolone-resistant bacteria in fecal samples. The method provides a robust tool for profiling bacterial genotypes at the single-cell level, facilitating the elucidation of microbial heterogeneity and its roles in complex populations.

title: Gut microbiota-CRAMP axis controls salivary gland immune homeostasis in Sjögren's disease.
abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder marked by lymphocytic infiltration of exocrine glands. To date, its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Cathelicidins are a widespread family of host-defense antimicrobial peptides, primarily recognized for their antimicrobial properties, and are now increasingly appreciated for their immunomodulatory functions. However, the role of cathelicidin in the immunopathogenesis of SjD remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the effects of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide (CRAMP) on SjD and the underlying mechanisms. Salivary gland tissues from SjD patients and controls were collected. Two established mouse models of SjD, i.e., the non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice that spontaneously develop SjD-like disease features, and salivary gland protein-induced experimental SjD mice, were used for the studies. Our data showed that salivary gland acinar cells produce cathelicidin, and that production is impaired in both SjD patients and mice compared to the control group. Moreover, CRAMP plays a protective role in SjD, as exogenous CRAMP administration improved the SjD phenotype, whereas CRAMP knockdown exacerbated disease severity. By combining RNA sequencing with pharmacological inhibitors, we demonstrated that CRAMP acts through formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) to inhibit the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, thereby reducing the autoimmune response in the salivary glands. Furthermore, we identified gut microbiota and its metabolite, propionic acid, as critical regulators of CRAMP expression in salivary gland acinar cells. Treatment with propionic acid or transfer of gut microbiota from a non-autoimmune control strain to SjD mice increased CRAMP levels and alleviated disease severity, highlighting a pivotal gut-salivary gland axis in SjD pathogenesis. Overall, these findings underscore the pivotal role of CRAMP in protecting against SjD and pave the way for future microbiota-based therapies.

title: Complete genomic sequence and characterization of Snakehead rhabdovirus -Indian strain (SHRV-In).
abstract: Rhabdoviruses are highly diverse RNA viruses that cause substantial economic losses in both wild and farmed fish populations. In this study, we determined the complete genome sequence of the snakehead rhabdovirus - Indian strain (SHRV-In), originally isolated from diseased snakehead fish with clinical symptoms of surface ulceration and high mortality. The viral genome is 11,550 nucleotides (11.55 kb) in length and contains 69 putative open reading frames (ORFs). Among these, six major ORFs are predicted to encode functional proteins, including RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (L), matrix protein (M), glycoprotein (G), non-virion protein (NV), phosphoprotein (P), and nucleoprotein (N), which are arranged in the conserved order of 3'-N-P-M-G-NV-L-5'. Comparative genomic analyses, including multiple sequence alignment, phylogenetic reconstruction, mutation identification, analysis of transcription signals, identification of conserved domains and comparative analysis of Untranslated regions (UTRs) revealed that SHRV-In shares significant homology with related fish rhabdoviruses but exhibits distinct genetic divergence from other snakehead rhabdovirus isolates. The whole genome exhibits a 96.11% sequence identity, and the phylogenetic analysis indicates a genetic divergence with SHRV, originating from Bethesda, USA and Corvallis, USA. Furthermore, Nucleoprotein (N) was identified as a promising vaccination candidate due to its high B-cell epitope scores and antigenic locations. Appraisal of the complete genome and the ORFs encoding structural proteins reveals considerable similarity with related fish rhabdovirus sequences and confirms the assignment of SHRV-In to the genus Novirhabdovirus. Overall, this study presents the first complete genomic characterisation of SHRV-In, providing insights into its evolutionary dynamics and establishing a foundation for future virological, epidemiological and disease-control studies in aquaculture.

title: METTL1-mediated tRNA m7G methylome remodeling drives macrophage M2 polarization and paclitaxel resistance in cervical cancer.
abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment of cervical cancer. Emerging evidence suggests that RNA methylation plays a crucial role in shaping tumor-immune interactions. However, the role of METTL1-mediated tRNA m7G modification in macrophage polarization and drug resistance is largely unexplored. Functional effects of METTL1 were examined through gain- and loss-of-function experiments in vitro, and xenograft models. Trac-seq was performed to characterize tRNA m7G remodeling. METTL1 was significantly upregulated in cervical cancer tissues and was predominantly expressed in macrophages within paclitaxel-resistant tumor samples. METTL1 overexpression promoted M2-like macrophage polarization, whereas METTL1 knockdown produced the opposite effects. METTL1-overexpressing macrophages enhanced cervical cancer cell proliferation and attenuated paclitaxel-induced cytotoxicity in vitro and promoted tumor growth under paclitaxel treatment in vivo. Trac-seq revealed extensive remodeling of tRNA m7G methylome following METTL1 overexpression, with selective hypo- and hypermethylation across distinct tRNAs. Single-cell analysis identified reduced NLRP3 expression in METTL1-high macrophages, and METTL1 overexpression suppressed pyroptosis, whereas WDR4 depletion produced opposing effects and partially attenuated METTL1-mediated changes in macrophages. METTL1 promotes M2-like macrophage polarization and paclitaxel resistance in cervical cancer, accompanied by extensive remodeling of the tRNA m7G methylome, providing a potential epitranscriptomic link between macrophage reprogramming and chemoresistance.

title: In-human assessment of target engagement and blockade of radiolabeled BI 765063, an anti-SIRPα antibody.
abstract: The signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPα) receptor on myeloid cells binds cluster of differentiation (CD) antigen CD47 on tumor cells, resulting in a "don't eat me" signal that inhibits phagocytosis. BI 765063, an anti-SIRPα antibody, may restore anti-tumor immunity by blocking this interaction. This phase I study aimed to assess target engagement and blockade of BI 765063 using quantitative 89Zr-immuno-PET, incorporating a previously developed correction method for non-target-mediated antibody catabolism. For this, four patients with advanced cancer received two cycles of [89Zr]Zr-BI 765063 and underwent three PET-scans per cycle up to 120 h post injection. The first cycle included a low dose of BI 765063 and the second a dose more than 20 times higher, intended to block the target. Directly after BI 765063 administration at the second cycle, ezabenlimab was administered to start the investigational treatment of the patients (BI 765063 + ezabenlimab, both every 3 weeks). Tumor uptake was corrected for antibody catabolism using literature-based reference values and normalized to plasma activity to calculate corrected tissue-to-plasma ratios (cTPR). Patlak analysis with the cTPR values yielded corrected net irreversible uptake rates (cKi). PET data were compared with RNA-sequencing data and macrophage marker immunohistochemistry. All ten tumor lesions showed target engagement by cTPR values at 120 h exceeding reference values. Positive cKi values were observed in all but one lesion, in which no Patlak analysis could be performed. cTPR values were lower for the blocking dose than the low dose, with five out of ten lesions within the range of non-target-mediated uptake, indicating partial target blockade. Target engagement observed by PET was supported by positive SIRPα mRNA expression and myeloid cell presence. Target engagement and blockade of BI 765063 were observed across all tumors, highlighting the potential of non-target-mediated antibody catabolism correction through cTPRs to improve quantification of target specific uptake with immuno-PET. ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05068102, Registered at 23 September 2021, https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05068102?term=NCT05068102.&rank=1.
authors: C Willemien Menke-van der Houven van Oordt

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis reveals molecular response characteristics to acute hypoxia stress in Culter alburnus.
abstract: Topmouth culter (Culter alburnus) is an economically important freshwater fish, yet the temporal responses of its liver to hypoxia stress remain poorly understood. This study investigated the changes in liver histological structure and antioxidant enzyme activities after different durations of hypoxia stress (L2H, L4H, L6H, L12H, and L24H). The results showed that the pathological damage gradually progressed from mild hepatic sinusoidal dilation to hepatocyte vacuolation. A significant decline in the antioxidant parameters (T-AOC, T-SOD, and CAT) was observed in the 6H group, which was followed by a slow rise. Furthermore, we performed a comparative analysis of the transcriptomes and metabolomes of the L6H, L24H, and control groups (LC). RNA-Seq analysis identified 2178 and 393 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the L6H-vs-LC and L24H-vs-LC groups, respectively. These DEGs were predominantly enriched in several pathways, including the HIF-1 signaling pathway, PPAR signaling pathway, and insulin signaling pathway. These findings suggested that hypoxia stress triggered a metabolic shift in C. alburnus through the enhanced efficiency of glycolytic energy supply. Metabolomic results revealed that 296 and 408 differential metabolites (DAMs) were identified in the L6H-vs-LC and L24H-vs-LC comparisons, respectively. These DAMs were mainly enriched in pathways associated with lipid remodeling, energy metabolism, and oxidative stress. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis revealed that the HIF-1 signaling pathway coordinately regulated gluconeogenesis, the pentose phosphate pathway, and glycerophospholipid metabolism. It cooperated with mTOR-mediated pathways and enhanced oxidative stress defense through FoxO family genes, thereby forming a multilayered metabolic adaptation network.
extra: Comp Biochem Physiol C Toxicol Pharmacol

title: Genome-wide characterization and analysis of the VviFBW gene family in regulating grape berry coloration.
abstract: F-box proteins serve as the substrate-recognition subunits of the SCF E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, playing pivotal roles in plant development, hormone signaling, and stress responses via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. However, a genome-wide characterization of the F-box/WD40 (FBW) subfamily in grapevine (Vitis vinifera L.) remains largely unexplored. In this study, we systematically identified and characterized eight FBW subfamily genes (designated as VviFBW1 to VviFBW8) in the grape genome. Phylogenetic analysis clustered these VviFBW proteins into three distinct subgroups alongside homologs from Arabidopsis and rice. Promoter analysis revealed an abundance of light-, stress-, and phytohormone-responsive cis-acting elements, suggesting that VviFBW genes are integrated into complex regulatory networks. Combined RNA-seq and RT-qPCR analyses revealed stage-specific expression profiles during fruit development; VviFBW8 was significantly upregulated during late ripening phases. The overexpression of VviFBW8 can promote the ripening and coloration of grape berry. Regulatory network analysis placed VviFBW genes at central nodes interacting with 84 transcription factors. Subcellular localization assays demonstrated that the VviFBW8 protein predominantly reside in the cytoplasm. GO enrichment analysis showed that VviFBW genes were mainly enriched in plant growth and hormone pathway. In summary, this study elucidate the evolutionary, structural, and expression characteristics of the VviFBW subfamily in grapevine, providing candidate target genes and a theoretical foundation for further deciphering the molecular mechanisms of FBW-mediated fruit development and stress adaptation.

title: Portable amplification-free diagnostics of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using SERS biosensor with machine learning-assisted classification.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the sixth most common cancer worldwide, with approximately 890,000 new cases annually, and is associated with disproportionately poor outcomes in low-resource settings due to limited access to early diagnostics and trained personnel. Bridging this gap requires transformative technologies that combine high sensitivity, minimal sample processing, and point-of-care access. Here, we present a portable platform for the direct detection of the mRNA biomarker keratin 14 (KRT14) in HNSCC based on a sandwich hybridization assay coupled with surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) using highly efficient probes: core-gap-shell spiky nanorattles (SpNRs). We systematically investigate the role of adenine spacer length on probe conformation on both magnetic beads (MBs) and SpNRs, as well as its effects on hybridization efficiency and SERS signal enhancement, identifying optimal configurations that enable a picomolar limit of detection without enzymatic amplification. Machine learning models based on the intensity of the characteristic Raman reporter band at 1358 cm⁻1 were used for quantification and classification, discriminating HNSCC from non-cancerous cell-line RNA. In a pilot set of clinical biopsies (two HNSCC patients, three healthy controls), we employed a support vector regression (SVR) classifier, which distinguished cancer from healthy tissue consistent with qRT-PCR, with CatBoost regression used for quantification. Overall, this work presents a nano-plasmonic sensing platform combined with machine learning analysis for nucleic acid detection, with potential applications in point-of-care cancer diagnostics.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology. Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences. Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis. Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

title: Zhenwu Decoction improves myocardial energy metabolism and mitochondrial integrity in pressure overload-induced heart failure partly through AMP-activated protein kinase signaling.
abstract: Zhenwu Decoction (ZWD), recorded in the Shang Han Lun, is traditionally used for yang deficiency with fluid retention, a pattern relevant to congestion and impaired cardiac function. Its mitochondrial mechanism in pressure-overload heart failure remains unclear. To evaluate the cardioprotective effects of ZWD and the contribution of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-related signaling. Male C57BL/6J mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction received low-, medium-, or high-dose ZWD (4.32, 8.64, or 17.28 g/kg/day, respectively) or the positive control captopril. Cardiac function, remodeling, oxidative stress, energy metabolites, mitochondrial ultrastructure, transcriptomics, and metabolomics were assessed. In angiotensin II-injured H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, small interfering RNA-mediated AMPK silencing was used to assess pathway dependence. ZWD improved systolic function and reduced ventricular dilation, injury biomarkers, collagen accumulation, and oxidative imbalance, with the most evident effects at the high dose. It increased adenosine triphosphate and acetyl-coenzyme A, reduced adenosine diphosphate and adenosine monophosphate, and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure. These changes were accompanied by increased AMPK phosphorylation and sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation. Multi-omics analyses identified treatment-associated changes in energy-related pathways. AMPK silencing attenuated, but did not completely abolish, the mitochondrial and metabolic effects of ZWD. ZWD ameliorated pressure-overload cardiac dysfunction and improved myocardial energy homeostasis and mitochondrial integrity. AMPK silencing partially attenuated the cellular response, supporting AMPK involvement in these protective effects, alongside increased sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation.

title: NeuroBase: A Web-Based Transcriptomic Resource and R Package for Cross-Disorder Analysis of Neurodegenerative and Neuropsychiatric Diseases.
abstract: Neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, autism spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder, Parkinson's disease, and schizophrenia, are highly prevalent and biologically complex conditions that remain difficult to diagnose and treat. This study aimed to develop NeuroBase, a web-based transcriptomic resource that supports exploratory comparison of shared and disorder-specific gene expression features across these disorders. Fourteen human brain bulk RNA sequencing datasets (262 total samples) were processed using a standardized pipeline, followed by differential gene expression analysis with DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom for broad exploratory discovery, complemented by a multi-method sensitivity analysis to define a method-concordant core gene set, protein-protein interaction network analysis using STRING with downstream exploration in Cytoscape, and functional enrichment analysis. Principal component analysis and clustering-based visualizations were used to summarize similarities and differences in transcriptomic patterns among disorders. Differential expression analysis identified dataset-level significant genes within each disorder using DESeq2 for one dataset per disorder (FDR ≤ 0.05), including 38 genes in Alzheimer's disease, 6,704 in autism spectrum disorder, 3,559 in bipolar disorder, 687 in Parkinson's disease, and 2,750 in schizophrenia; a stricter multi-method intersection analysis yielded method-concordant Core Intersection sets in the most informative datasets (983 core DEGs in autism spectrum disorder, 505 in bipolar disorder, 281 in schizophrenia, and 234 and 151 in two Parkinson's disease datasets; only two core genes (SPP1 and CHST3) were found in Alzheimer's disease). A unified strict-threshold reanalysis (FDR ≤ 0.05, |log₂FC|≥ 1) revealed disorder-level DEG burdens ranging from 34 (Alzheimer's disease) to 2,812 (autism) deduplicated genes, but only 24 genes were reproducible across independent cohorts of the same disorder, highlighting the limited cross-cohort reproducibility characteristic of bulk brain transcriptomics. Enrichment analyses identified significantly enriched signaling pathways in autism spectrum disorder and nominally enriched synapse-related pathways in Alzheimer's disease. Representative high-signal genes included SPP1 in Alzheimer's disease, NRGN in one Parkinson's disease dataset, and BEST1 in autism spectrum disorder. Cross-disorder comparison identified 465 differentially expressed genes shared between the neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorder groups, and principal component analysis showed that sample variation was dominated by dataset and tissue of origin. NeuroBase is a publicly accessible, web-based transcriptomic database and companion R package (neurobaseR) that enables standardized, cross-disorder exploration of bulk brain gene expression profiles across neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders, supporting comparative analysis, programmatic data access, and hypothesis generation through interactive visualization and pathway-level summaries.

title: Immune-fibroblast ligand-receptor axes in post-infarction cardiac remodeling: convergent and divergent mechanisms compared with cancer-associated fibroblasts.
abstract: Myocardial infarction-triggered cardiac fibrosis is a cardinal feature of maladaptive ventricular remodeling and a principal contributor to heart failure pathogenesis. Enabled by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, accumulating evidence demonstrates that post-infarction fibrosis represents an actively coordinated biological program rather than a passive wound-healing event, which is governed by ligand-receptor-mediated crosstalk between immune cells and cardiac fibroblasts. Pioneering work has established monocyte-derived macrophages as a predominant cellular source of pro-inflammatory interleukin-1β; upon binding its cognate receptor on fibroblasts, this cytokine instigates the generation of pro-fibrotic fibroblast subsets within spatially segregated niches of the infarcted myocardium. Multiple additional ligand-receptor modules, encompassing osteopontin-CD44/integrin, transforming growth factor-β, platelet-derived growth factor, as well as growth arrest-specific protein 6-MER tyrosine kinase, further fine-tune fibroblast activation trajectories in a spatiotemporally-restricted fashion. Intriguingly, a substantial fraction of these ligand-receptor interactions are conserved in cancer-associated fibroblast biology, wherein osteopontin-producing macrophages and activated fibroblasts collaboratively build pro-tumor stromal microenvironments. We consolidate recent multi-omic findings regarding immune-fibroblast ligand-receptor communication during post-infarction cardiac remodeling, highlight mechanistic analogies to cancer-associated fibroblast activation, and discuss therapeutic prospects arising from targeting these conserved signaling nodes across cardiac and neoplastic diseases.

title: Targeting CCR7 Attenuates Aggressive Phenotypes in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma by Suppressing Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling.
abstract: The CCL21/CCR7 chemokine axis is implicated in lymphocyte trafficking and cancer metastasis, yet its specific role and molecular mechanism in the pathogenesis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remain poorly defined. CCR7 expression was assessed in clinical samples by immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry. In vitro functional assays and molecular techniques were employed in DLBCL cell lines to investigate the CCL21/CCR7 axis. Downstream mechanisms were investigated through RNA sequencing, Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and rescue experiments using the Wnt/β-catenin inhibitor XAV-939. CCR7 was significantly overexpressed in aggressive DLBCL and correlated with advanced disease stage and poor prognosis. The CCL21/CCR7 axis significantly promoted tumor cell migration, invasion, resistance to apoptosis, and mesenchymal-like phenotypic changes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed the Wnt/β-catenin pathway as the most significantly enriched downstream target. Mechanistically, CCL21/CCR7 activation was associated with enhanced Wnt/β-catenin signaling and a potential physical association between CCR7 and β-catenin-containing protein complexes. Inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling attenuated CCL21-induced malignant phenotypes. As a potential therapeutic intervention, the anti-CCR7 monoclonal antibody CAP-100 attenuated CCR7-associated signaling, inhibited Wnt/β-catenin activation, reversed mesenchymal-like phenotypic changes, and suppressed the malignant behaviors of DLBCL cells in vitro. Our study provides novel insights into DLBCL pathogenesis by suggesting that the CCL21/CCR7 axis contributes to tumor aggressiveness at least partly through activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, leading to mesenchymal-like phenotypic remodeling. These findings support CCR7 as a potential therapeutic target and suggest that antibody-mediated CCR7 blockade warrants further in vivo validation.

title: A de novo IKZF4 Variant Underlies Hypogammaglobulinemia and Increased Infection Susceptibility through Downregulating the NF-κB Pathway.
abstract: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) are a group of complex diseases characterized by reduced immunity and increased susceptibility to external pathogens, autoinflammation, autoimmune conditions, and/or malignancy. The IKAROS zinc-finger (IKZF) family is a group of C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factors that includes IKAROS (IKZF1), HELIOS (IKZF2), AIOLOS (IKZF3), EOS (IKZF4), and PEGASUS (IKZF5). Variants in IKZF have been reported to cause human IEI except IKZF4. This research aimed to identify the pathogenicity and underlying mechanisms of IKZF4 as a novel candidate gene for IEI. Here, we used whole-exome sequencing to identify candidate variants of IEI. Western blotting, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, immune staining, co-immunoprecipitation, flow cytometry, Luminex assays, and single-cell RNA sequencing were used to explore the phenotypes and functional effects in cell and mouse models. An 11-month-old patient presented with repeated fever and convulsions accompanied by persistently reduced immunoglobulin levels and abnormal immune indices, which supported the diagnosis of IEI. A de novo c.1472delG variant (GRCh37/hg19, NM_022465.3) in IKZF4 was selected as the candidate variant for IEI. The c.1472delG variant caused reduced EOS expression and truncated protein (predicted molecular weight ~ 57 kDa), defective pericentromeric heterochromatin targeting, and impaired protein interactions of EOS. A mouse model harboring the corresponding variant in Ikzf4 (Ikzf4+/c.1475delG) showed a proinflammatory switch in regulatory T cells, accompanied by reduced levels of immunoglobulins and a decreased ratio of marginal zone B cells after lipopolysaccharide stimulation, which were potentially caused by the down-regulated transcriptional regulation of EOS on the nuclear factor kappa-B pathway. This research identified IKZF4 as a novel candidate gene for IEI, advancing our knowledge of the IKZF family and the complexity of human IEI.

title: Protocol for integrated multimodal spatial RNA and protein profiling using Xenium and MACSima.
abstract: Combining same-section spatial transcriptomics with high-plex protein imaging enables comprehensive characterization of the tissue microenvironment while preserving spatial information. Here, we present a protocol for multimodal spatial RNA and protein profiling using Xenium transcriptomics and MACSima cyclic protein imaging. We describe steps for tissue preparation, hybridization, and RNA imaging, followed by slide recovery, antigen retrieval, and MACSima imaging cyclic staining (MICS). We provide Python scripts for data registration and integration to generate a single-cell multimodal map of the tissue microenvironment.

title: KDM4B Knockdown Attenuates Neurological Deficits in Ischemic Stroke by Inhibiting Neuronal Apoptosis Associated With Birc5 Upregulation.
abstract: KDM4B (Lysine demethylase 4B), a histone lysine demethylase, exerts a crucial epigenetic regulatory role in the progression of numerous disorders by catalyzing demethylation reactions on target proteins. However, the precise biological function and molecular mechanism by which KDM4B regulates neurological deficits in ischemic stroke remains elusive. In this study, we employed a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in HT22 neurons to mimic ischemic stroke. Targeted loss-of-function approaches were executed utilizing in vivo siRNA delivery and in vitro lentiviral shRNA transduction. The neuroprotective effects were systematically evaluated through infarct volume quantification, histopathological staining, and diverse sensorimotor behavioral tests. Furthermore, transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq) coupled with molecular biology assays was performed to elucidate the downstream apoptotic cascades and key targets governed by KDM4B. Herein, we found that KDM4B is predominantly localized in neurons, with its expression significantly decreasing initially and then gradually increasing following ischemic stroke. Loss-of-function experiments demonstrated that KDM4B knockdown mitigated brain damage, attenuated tissue structure disruption, and improved sensorimotor dysfunctions in mice with ischemic stroke. Additionally, KDM4B knockdown protected neurons against OGD/R insult. Furthermore, KDM4B knockdown inhibited the expression of Bax and the activation of the pro-apoptotic caspase cascade (caspase-3/6/7/8/9), while upregulating the expression of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, thereby reducing neuronal apoptosis. Mechanistically, KDM4B knockdown is associated with an upregulation of Birc5 expression, which in turn inhibits apoptotic progression in neurons. These results demonstrate that KDM4B knockdown alleviates neurological deficits following ischemic stroke by inhibiting neuronal apoptosis, partially accompanied by Birc5.

title: From histopathology to molecular taxonomy: predicting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors invasiveness.
abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are among the most prevalent intracranial tumors in adults. Although most follow an indolent clinical course, a substantial subset exhibits local invasion, which can limit gross total resection and increase the risk of residual disease and recurrence. Importantly, anatomical invasiveness should not be equated with clinical aggressiveness. Aggressive PitNETs may also exhibit a longitudinal pattern of repeated or multiple local recurrences and frequently require multiple therapeutic interventions. The 2022 Fifth Edition of the WHO Classification formally renamed pituitary adenomas to PitNETs and established a lineage classification framework centered on core transcription factors, including PIT1, TPIT, and SF1, thereby driving the transition from traditional pathological diagnosis to molecular subtyping. Driven by recent advances in high-throughput sequencing, liquid biopsy, and single-cell omics, numerous novel molecular biomarkers have emerged, enabling the early pre- and postoperative identification of invasive subpopulations. This review systematically outlines recent progress in multidimensional biomarkers-including DNA methylation, protein markers, non-coding RNAs, liquid biopsy indicators, and tumor microenvironmental features-to provide an updated synthesis of candidate biomarkers that may support future risk stratification and individualized management of invasive PitNETs.

title: RNA sequencing depth guidelines for the study of alternative splicing.
abstract: A key parameter in the experimental design of RNA-seq projects is the choice of sequencing depth. Considering a limited budget, one needs to find a trade-off between the number of samples and the sensitivity of the analysis, particularly concerning lowly expressed genes. While previous studies have proposed a lower bound for the comprehensive analysis of differential gene expression, for the analysis of alternative splicing, it has only been proposed for human adipose tissue. However, alternative splicing differs across tissues and conditions. We analyzed publicly available and newly generated deep-sequenced paired-end RNA-seq samples (between 150 and >500 million reads, read length 50-150 bp) from human buffy coat cells and diverse sets of tissues, including gluteal subcutaneous fat, heart, and hypothalamus. Our results show that the sequencing depth typically used in published cohorts is not sufficient to comprehensively capture the landscape of alternative splicing. This motivates the use of deeper sequencing or long-read technologies in future studies. Toward this goal, we offer guidelines and a website (https://sequencing-depth4splicing.com/) for choosing a suitable sequencing depth.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and in silico analysis identifies novel long non-coding RNAs associated with BCL6 and SPARC in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
abstract: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common and clinically heterogeneous subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, marked by extensive transcriptional dysregulation and variable therapeutic outcomes. While protein-coding alterations are well characterized, the regulatory role of the non-coding transcriptome remains incompletely defined. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) modulate gene expression through cis/trans transcriptional control, RNA-RNA interactions, and RNA-protein scaffolding. However, DLBCL-specific lncRNAs remain largely unexplored. We applied an integrative in silico framework using RNA-seq datasets from the Sequence Read Archive and The Cancer Genome Atlas, incorporating quality control, alignment, quantification, TPM normalization, differential expression, principal component analysis, multi-level filtering, cis-annotation, survival analysis, functional enrichment with STRING network construction, mutation profiling, RNA-RNA interaction prediction (IntaRNA), and RNA-protein interaction analysis (catRAPID) with structural modeling. With this approach we identified three previously uncharacterized lncRNAs, namely lnc-SPARC-2:3, lnc-FXYD2-1:5, and lnc-ADAMTS1-2:1. These consistently overexpressed lncRNAs in DLBCL were validated by semi-quantitative PCR. In silico thermodynamic modeling supported stable RNA-RNA duplex formation with neighboring mRNAs, and protein interaction analyses predicted high-confidence binding to BCL6 protein. These lncRNAs are predicted to participate in lncRNA-mediated attenuation of BCL6 and may disrupt germinal center regulatory programs, impair B-cell lineage commitment and promote microenvironment-dependent signaling, alongside enrichment of ECM proteoglycans indicative of stromal remodeling, accompanied by marked upregulation of SPARC mRNA. Correlation analyses across the SRA and TCGA cohorts supported the IntaRNA-predicted interactions of lnc-ADAMTS1-2:1-ADAMTS5, lnc-FXYD2-1:5-FXYD6, and lnc-SPARC-2:3-ATOX1, revealing consistent positive associations that remained supported after adjustment for cohort and stromal score. Notably, the observed survival trend for lnc-FXYD2-1:5 did not reach statistical significance; nevertheless, it is suggested as a candidate biomarker with potential prognostic relevance that merits further investigation in larger independent cohorts. Collectively, this study provides a systematic computational framework supported by experimental validation for the presence of the shortlisted lncRNAs. However, further experimental validation is required to establish their functional roles, which may support their investigation as potential therapeutic targets in future DLBCL studies.

title: SPROUT Guidelines for Molecular Profiling for Children with Solid Tumors: A Consensus Recommendation from the American Association for Cancer Research.
abstract: Molecular diagnostics are standard of care for most adults with solid malignancies, but implementation in pediatric solid tumors remains inconsistent. The SPROUT (Somatic Profiling for Pediatric Cancer Refining our Understanding and Treatment) Molecular Guidelines Working Group was convened to develop molecular testing guidelines for pediatric solid tumors. A structured literature review was performed using Covidence to identify relevant clinical studies evaluating molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. The literature and collective clinical experience of the multidisciplinary working group were used to develop consensus recommendations for molecular profiling at diagnosis and at relapse or recurrence. Of 361 manuscripts screened, 41 studies were included for data extraction. Based on the available evidence and expert consensus, recommendations were developed for the use and timing of DNA and RNA next-generation sequencing and methylation profiling across pediatric solid tumors. The SPROUT Molecular Guidelines provide a framework for standardized implementation of molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. Broad adoption of these recommendations may improve diagnostic precision, reduce variability in molecular testing, and increase opportunities for biomarker-directed therapy and clinical trial enrollment for children with cancer.

title: Transcriptomic changes associated with the antiproliferative effects of indole-3-acetic acid in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells: an exploratory study.
abstract: Neuroblastoma is a highly heterogeneous paediatric malignancy characterized by dysregulated oncogenic pathways that promote tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. We previously demonstrated that indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), a naturally occurring indole derivative, exerts antiproliferative effects in SH-SY5Y and SK-N-BE(2) neuroblastoma cells by reducing cell viability, downregulating ALK expression, inducing G1 cell-cycle arrest, promoting autophagy, and suppressing clonogenicity and migration. To explore molecular correlates of these effects, we analysed the transcriptomic response of SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells to IAA treatment by RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), followed by differential expression analysis and Gene Ontology (GO)-based Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA). RNA-seq identified concentration-dependent transcriptional responses to IAA treatment, with the most pronounced changes observed at 1 mM concentration. GSEA identified neuronal migration as a significantly enriched biological process, suggesting modulation of developmental programs associated with the neural origin of neuroblastoma cells. Among the differentially expressed genes, ERBB4 and GPM6A showed reduced expression and MAMDC2 displayed increased expression following IAA treatment, changes that were confirmed by qRT-PCR in independent biological samples. ADGRG1, FER1L4 and DCDC2 were not confirmed by qRT-PCR and are reported as RNA-seq observations only. ALK transcript levels remained unaffected, raising the hypothesis that reduced ALK protein levels may involve post-transcriptional regulation, although this was not directly tested in the present study. ERBB4, MAMDC2 and GPM6A are involved in cancer-related signalling and cellular behaviour, and their modulation by IAA has not been previously described. These findings show that IAA induces extensive transcriptional changes in SH-SY5Y cells and identify candidate molecular correlates of its antiproliferative activity. This exploratory, hypothesis-generating study is limited to transcript-level data from a single cell line. It provides a dataset and candidate genes for future validation and mechanistic studies in neuroblastoma models with different molecular backgrounds.

title: Connexin43 Links Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells to Peripheral Adiposity in Female Mice Under HFD.
abstract: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are a major source of bone marrow adipose tissue and also contribute to the total adipocyte pool under high-fat diet (HFD) challenge, yet the underlying molecular links are uncertain. Given that connexin 43 (Cx43), a key gap junction protein, regulates BMSC differentiation and energy metabolism, we aimed to determine its effects on BMSCs in controlling peripheral adipose tissue under HFD. BMSC-specific Cx43 knockout (Prrx1-Cre; Cx43flox/flox, cKO) and control littermates (Cx43flox/flox, flox) were fed either a control diet or a HFD for 8 weeks. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to profile BMSC subclusters and identify HFD-responsive clusters and their secreted factors. We observed that cKO mice displayed resistance to HFD-induced body adiposity and enhanced energy expenditure, an effect that was particularly pronounced in females. Two new clusters (Prrx1+Ly6a+ and Adipoq+Clec11a+) were identified, which contribute to Cx43 ablation against HFD. Cx43 inhibition links reduced adipogenesis to lower TXNIP secretion in serum. Lastly, TXNIP inhibition recapitulates the lean phenotype of cKO mice under HFD. Our data appear to support a link between BMSC Cx43 and TXNIP secretion within a bone-adipose axis, which might be relevant to addressing challenges in obesity management.

title: [Kinesin family member 26A inhibits colorectal cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and migration by regulating the JunB-mediated PI3K-AKT signaling pathway].
abstract: Objective: To investigate the regulatory role of Kinesin family member 26A (KIF26A) in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell invasion and migration and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanism. Methods: Bioinformatics analysis using TCGA databases was performed to assess the correlation between KIF26A expression and clinic pathological characteristics. Flow cytometry was employed to examine the effect of KIF26A on cell cycle distribution. Transwell assays were conducted to evaluate the impact of KIF26A on CRC cell invasion and migration. RNA-seq, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), Western blot, Co-Immunoprecipitation (Co-IP)and Chromatin Immunoprecipitation followed by qPCR (ChIP-qPCR) were utilized to explore the downstream regulatory network and molecular mechanisms. Results: Following KIF26A knockdown, the G0/G1 phase proportion in HCT116 cells decreased from (75.80±0.64)% in the negative control group to (73.57±0.53)% and (72.17±0.08)% in the shKIF26A#1 and shKIF26A#2 groups, respectively (both P＜0.05); the number of invasive cells increased from 192.60±4.50 to 483.00±6.74 and 471.80±8.01, respectively (both P＜0.001); and the number of migratory cells increased from 288.40±4.39 to 489.20±5.58 and 490.40±7.17, respectively (both P＜0.001). In RKO cells, the G0/G1 phase proportion decreased from (61.17±0.41)% in the negative control group to (57.13±0.23)% and (57.70±0.06)% in the shKIF26A#1 and shKIF26A#2 groups, respectively (both P＜0.001); the number of invasive cells increased from 57.60±4.11 to 160.80±5.48 and 136.20±4.44, respectively (both P＜0.001); and the number of migratory cells increased from 81.00±2.95 to 270.80±4.42 and 299.00±3.63, respectively (both P＜0.001). Following KIF26A overexpression, the G0/G1 phase proportion in HCT116 cells increased from (41.20±0.88)% in the empty vector control group to (54.33±0.33)% in the KIF26A overexpression group (P<0.001); the number of invasive cells decreased from 338.00±5.57 to 194.80±4.90 (P＜0.001); and the number of migratory cells decreased from 408.60±3.33 to 263.60±3.59 (P＜0.001). In RKO cells, the G0/G1 phase proportion increased from (57.63±0.33)% in the empty vector control group to (62.65±0.45)% in the KIF26A overexpression group (P＜0.001); the number of invasive cells decreased from 102.60±3.37 to 54.80±2.01 (P＜0.001); and the number of migratory cells decreased from 180.00±4.18 to 90.40±4.77 (P＜0.001). GSEA of differentially expressed genes between KIF26A-high and KIF26A-low expression groups in TCGA samples, as well as between KIF26A-overexpressing RKO cells and empty vector controls, revealed significant enrichment of differentially expressed genes in pathways related to cell cycle, invasion, and migration (all P＜0.05). Mechanistic studies revealed that KIF26A knockdown suppressed the expression of retinoblastoma protein (RB) and E2F transcription factor 1 (E2F1) in colon cancer cells while promoting the expression of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (AKT1); conversely, KIF26A overexpression promoted RB and E2F1 expression and inhibited PI3K and AKT1 expression. Co-IP combined with mass spectrometry identified JunB as an interacting protein of KIF26A. ChIP assay results showed that JunB binds to the promoter region of PTEN. Rescue experiments demonstrated that JunB knockdown partially reversed the inhibition of invasion and migration mediated by KIF26A overexpression (P＜0.001). Conclusions: KIF26A regulates cell cycle progression through the RB/E2F1 pathway and modulates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway via interaction with JunB, thereby inhibiting the invasion and migration of colorectal cancer cells. The elucidation of the KIF26A-JunB-PI3K-AKT regulatory axis provides a novel perspective for understanding the mechanisms of tumor metastasis, and KIF26A may serve as a potential predictive biomarker and therapeutic target for tumor metastasis.

title: 5'tRF-32-Glu promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression and has diagnostic value in serum.
abstract: To assess the diagnostic relevance of serum 5'tRF-32-Glu and its potential role to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. High-throughput sequencing of paired HCC and non-tumor tissues was used to identify candidate transfer RNA-derived small RNAs. Serum 5'tRF-32-Glu was subsequently quantified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and its molecular identity was verified by agarose gel electrophoresis and Sanger sequencing. Diagnostic performance and associations with clinicopathological features were assessed in a clinical cohort, including analyses of HCC, healthy controls, hepatitis controls, and BCLC 0/A HCC. Its effects on HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth were examined in vitro and in vivo. Serum 5'tRF-32-Glu levels were higher in the HCC group than in healthy controls and patients with hepatitis, whereas surgical resection was accompanied by a marked reduction in circulating levels. Higher serum expression was associated with tumor size, tumor number, BCLC stage, and Child-Pugh class. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 5'tRF-32-Glu was 0.714, and combining it with alpha-fetoprotein and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist-II increased the area under the curve to 0.884 and the sensitivity increased to 96%. Functionally, 5'tRF-32-Glu promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while its inhibition suppressed xenograft growth. Serum 5'tRF-32-Glu shows potential as a circulating HCC biomarker and may complement established markers for improved detection. Its functional effects on malignant phenotypes further support its potential role in the progress of HCC.

title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics links amino acid metabolism-related biomarkers to endothelial immune remodeling in periodontitis.
abstract: Periodontitis (PD) is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by microbial dysbiosis and immune-mediated periodontal tissue destruction. Although amino acid metabolic dysregulation has been implicated in inflammatory diseases, its diagnostic relevance and cellular context in PD remain unclear. We aimed to identify amino acid metabolism-related diagnostic biomarkers and characterize their potential roles in PD. Bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE16134, GSE10334, and GSE223924) and a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset (GSE164241) were analyzed. Amino acid metabolism-related differentially expressed genes were identified and functionally annotated through enrichment analyses. LASSO regression, Boruta, and random forest jointly screened diagnostic biomarkers. A nomogram was constructed and assessed by ROC, calibration, and decision curve analyses. Immune infiltration, consensus clustering, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed; cell-type localization, cell-cell communication, and pseudotime analyses used single-cell data. Human gingival tissue samples were used for validation through histological analysis, immunohistochemistry, and quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR). Six amino acid metabolism-related biomarkers showed concordant expression changes across the three bulk datasets. TDO2, ICAM2, VWF and FABP4 were upregulated in periodontitis, whereas ACAT2 and AHNAK2 were downregulated. The six-gene nomogram discriminated PD from controls in GSE16134 (AUC = 0.956), while cross-platform evaluation revealed calibration limitations. Enrichment analysis linked these biomarkers to chemokine and cytokine signaling, cell adhesion and leukocyte transendothelial migration. Immune infiltration and consensus clustering revealed broad immune associations and three expression-based subgroups with distinct inflammatory features. Single-cell analysis localized the highest biomarker activity to endothelial cells, which showed the strongest diagnostic biomarker module score despite a relative reduction in their proportion. Pseudotime analysis revealed biomarker expression variation along an inferred endothelial trajectory, while CellChat predicted altered endothelial-immune communication. Experimental validation confirmed these changes for TDO2, ICAM2, VWF, FABP4 and ACAT2 at both mRNA and protein levels in clinical samples. We identify six amino acid metabolism-related candidate biomarkers with diagnostic potential for PD-five supported by clinical gingival tissue expression data-and link them to endothelial cell state changes and immune microenvironment remodeling. These findings provide an immune-metabolic framework for biomarker development and mechanistic studies in PD.

title: Maternal late-pregnancy BMI is associated with compartment-specific immune-metabolic signatures across the maternal-placental-fetal axis.
abstract: Elevated maternal body mass index (BMI) during pregnancy is associated with adverse maternal and offspring outcomes; yet the molecular pathways linking maternal metabolic status to placental function and fetal immune development remain poorly understood. We performed multi-compartment transcriptomic profiling across the maternal-placental-fetal axis, complemented by exploratory cytokine profiling in a larger available plasma sample set. Maternal peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), placental villous tissue, cord blood mononuclear cells (CBMCs), maternal plasma, and cord plasma were collected at delivery when available. RNA-seq data were available for 17 maternal PBMC samples, 18 CBMC samples, and 14 placental samples from 20 term pregnancies, while Luminex profiling was performed in 31 maternal plasma and 31 cord plasma samples, comprising available plasma from the RNA-seq cohort plus additional plasma-only samples. RNA-seq analyses were performed separately within each compartment using third-trimester BMI as a continuous variable, followed by Hallmark pathway enrichment, co-expression network analysis, cytokine/chemokine profiling and targeted placental qRT-PCR validation. Higher maternal third-trimester BMI was associated with distinct transcriptional programs across maternal, placental, and fetal compartments. In maternal PBMCs, higher third-trimester BMI was associated with a modest but coordinated gene-level signature and pathway patterns consistent with selective immune activation, alongside broader attenuation of metabolic, inflammatory, and redox-related programs. Placental tissue exhibited the strongest BMI-associated transcriptomic signature, characterized by metabolic and stress-response activation, including enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, reactive oxygen species signaling, unfolded protein response, DNA repair, MTORC1 signaling, and adipogenesis. Exploratory co-expression analyses further highlighted candidate extracellular matrix, vascular-interface, and placental endocrine-associated modules. In CBMCs, higher third-trimester BMI was associated with fetal immune-developmental remodeling, including proliferative pathway enrichment and relative attenuation of inflammatory and immune-response signaling. Exploratory plasma cytokine profiling identified nominal compartment-specific associations with higher third-trimester BMI; however, none remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Collectively, the multi-compartment findings nominate candidate mitochondrial, inflammatory, vascular-interface, extracellular matrix, and placental endocrine-associated pathways for validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Transcriptomic Characterization of Cellular Senescence in Human Donor Livers Before Transplantation.
abstract: With an aging donor population, ischemic and inflammatory injury during organ procurement and preservation may be associated with senescence-associated programs influencing graft biology. Although donor type-specific injury patterns are known, their role in driving cellular senescence and downstream inflammatory responses remains unclear. We performed smart-3SEQ bulk RNA-sequencing on human liver tissue obtained from donation after brain death (DBD) and donation after circulatory death (DCD) donors. Senescence-associated transcriptional signatures were assessed using the SenMayo gene panel and a liver-specific senescence-associated secretory phenotype panel. Immunohistochemistry assessed p16 and p21 protein expression. Findings were evaluated in NanoString-based transcriptomic data from an external cohort. Sixty-six livers (24 DBD and 42 DCD) were included. One thousand five hundredforty-eight differentially expressed genes separated DBD and DCD grafts. Functional enrichment analysis showed distinct biological programs, with DBD grafts enriched for metabolic pathways, epithelial proliferation, and angiogenesis regulation, whereas DCD grafts showed enrichment of immune activation, chemokine signaling, and injury-associated pathways. Senescence-associated analyzes recapitulated this separation. Immunohistochemistry showed a higher proportion of p16-positive nuclei in high-risk DCD livers compared with DBD livers (p = 0.038), whereas no significant difference was observed for p21 (p = 0.687). However, tile-level analysis showed significantly higher proportions of both p16- and p21-positive nuclei in DCD livers (p < 0.001). External cohort analysis confirmed donor-type separation across available transcripts and senescence-associated gene panels. Donor type reflects distinct transcriptional states in human donor livers, with senescence-associated profiles overlapping with donor type-specific injury responses. Injury-induced senescence-associated signaling may influence graft function and recipient (patho)physiology, positioning it as a promising modifiable senolytic or senomorphic target in liver transplantation.

title: Periostin regulation by CEBPB and RACK1 and the effects of periostin-rich exosomes in osteoarthritis models.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) involves chondrocyte stress and disrupted intercellular communication, but the proteins associated with synovial fluid-derived exosomes remain incompletely defined. We investigated periostin regulation in chondrocyte models and cellular responses relevant to OA following exposure to periostin-rich exosomes. Exosomes isolated from synovial fluid samples from 15 patients with OA and 5 healthy volunteers (K-L grade 0) were analyzed using label-free proteomics. Human cartilage single-cell transcriptomic data, chondrocyte stress and serial-passage models, promoter-reporter assays, co-immunoprecipitation, protein-turnover assays, RNA sequencing, pathway-inhibition experiments, and destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) studies were used for follow-up. Exploratory proteomics identified periostin as a candidate protein, whose abundance was also elevated in models associated with chondrocyte senescence. CEBPB increased periostin expression and POSTN promoter-reporter activity. RACK1 co-precipitated with periostin; RACK1 overexpression slowed periostin degradation and reduced its ubiquitination. Periostin-rich exosomes increased chondrocyte catabolic activity and senescence-associated changes, increased macrophage inflammatory markers, and increased endothelial cell migration and tube formation in vitro. In DMM mice, intra-articular delivery of short hairpin RNA (shRNA) constructs targeting Cebpb or Rack1 reduced cartilage damage, whereas periostin-rich exosome supplementation partially attenuated these effects. Representative joint-tissue immunoblots showed lower CEBPB or RACK1 expression in the corresponding shRNA groups and higher periostin abundance following exosome supplementation. A p38 inhibitor or a MEK/ERK inhibitor partially attenuated chondrocyte responses to exosome treatment. CEBPB promotes periostin expression, whereas RACK1 increases periostin protein stability and contributes to p38/ERK-associated responses to periostin-rich exosomes in chondrocyte models. Intra-articular targeting of Cebpb or Rack1 reduced cartilage damage in DMM mice.

title: A field-deployable colorimetric reverse transcription-LAMP assay for the detection of a prostate cancer biomarker.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is becoming increasingly common in males worldwide, and early identification is crucial for improved patient prognosis and therapeutic results. Messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) are promising noninvasive biomarkers for PCa diagnosis because they can be extracted from various body fluids. Yes-Associated Protein 1 (YAP1) mRNA is a biomarker for PCa diagnosis and is highly expressed in human PCa cells. Herein, the ability of RT-LAMP and a visual platform to detect YAP1 mRNA for PCa diagnosis was explored. For the first time, the color behavior of a charge-transfer complex (oxTMB) was investigated to detect a PCa biomarker. Due to the electrostatic interactions between the positively-charged oxTMB and the negatively-charged LAMP amplicons, oxTMB was not reduced even when the potential reductant, dopamine (DA), was added. Consequently, the green color of oxTMB was retained under electrostatic interactions, whereas oxTMB in the negative sample was reduced, and the green color disappeared. The introduced oxTMB/DA-based LAMP approach showed high selectivity and a visual limit of detection of the PCa biomarker at 3.64 × 104 copies/μL in a cultured DU-145 cell line-derived RNA sample. Owing to its simplicity, rapidity, and practical viability, this oxTMB/DA-based colorimetric approach could be employed to detect PCa biomarkers in resource-limited areas.

title: Epigenetic-Transcriptional Signatures Associated with Carapace Length Variation in Mud Crab Scylla paramamosain.
abstract: Carapace length is an important growth-related trait in the mud crab Scylla paramamosain, yet its epigenetic and transcriptional basis remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from muscle tissues of mud crabs exhibiting extreme carapace length phenotypes. We identified 2,046 differentially methylated genes (DMGs) and 114 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Exploratory functional analyses suggested potential involvement of DMGs in metabolic regulation, molecular transport, signal transduction and cytoskeletal organization, whereas DEGs enrichment analysis highlighted proteasome-related functions with significant enrichment after multiple-testing correction. Integrated methylome-transcriptome analysis identified seven genes showing both differential methylation and differential expression, among which CycG, AGBE, Prosalpha5 and mucin-2-like (LOC135108177) were prioritized as candidate genes associated with carapace length variation. These genes showed distinct methylation-expression patterns and were linked to cell-cycle regulation, glycogen metabolism, proteasome-mediated protein turnover and glycoprotein-related processes. Multi-tissue RNA-seq profiling further revealed distinct relative tissue expression trends of these candidates, with CycG and AGBE showing relatively higher expression in eyestalk, Prosalpha5 in ovary and muscle, and mucin-2-like (LOC135108177) in eyestalk and testis. Together, these findings suggest that methylation-associated transcriptional variation may contribute to muscle molecular responses associated with carapace length variation in S. paramamosain. This study provides a genome-wide view of epigenetic-transcriptional associations underlying growth-related morphological variation in crustaceans and offers candidate molecular resources for future genetic improvement of mud crab.

title: Comprehensive characterization of the cellular and molecular consequences of LCN2 loss in MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer cells.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive breast cancer subtype characterized by high metastatic potential and limited targeted therapeutic options. Lipocalin-2 (LCN2) has been implicated in tumor progression and metastatic dissemination, but its functional role in TNBC remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the role of LCN2 in the human TNBC cell line MDA-MB-231. Stable LCN2-deficient (LCN2KO) cells were generated using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, followed by isolation of single-cell-derived clones. RNA sequencing was performed to characterize transcriptomic changes, with selected findings validated by reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Western blotting was used to assess protein-level changes. Transwell migration and invasion assays and adhesion assays were performed to evaluate functional effects. LCN2KO cells largely retained the mesenchymal phenotype of parental cells. RNA sequencing revealed changes associated with inflammatory signaling, iron homeostasis, oxidative stress, ferroptosis-related processes, and cellular metabolism. Functional assays demonstrated reduced migration, invasion, and adhesion, accompanied by altered adhesion to extracellular matrix components. LCN2 deficiency is associated with transcriptional and functional changes in MDA-MB-231 cells, particularly affecting migratory and invasive behavior and cell-matrix interactions, while largely preserving the mesenchymal phenotype. These findings provide further insight into the role of LCN2 in cellular processes relevant to TNBC progression and metastatic behavior.

title: Fractalkine produced by Shiga toxin type 2-stimulated human glomerular endothelial cells modulates γδ T lymphocyte migration.
abstract: γδ T cells play a critical role in tissue immunosurveillance through their capacity to sense cellular stress. However, their recruitment dynamics to peripheral organs such as kidney during Shiga toxin (Stx)-induced renal damage, remain undefined. Since the CX3CL1/CX3CR1 axis is vital for leukocyte homing into inflamed organs, we investigated its participation in mediating γδ T cell trafficking to the Stx-damaged kidney. We integrated in vitro functional assays using Stx2a-stimulated human glomerular endothelial cells (HGEC) with in silico single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis of public human kidney injury datasets. CX3CL1/CX3CR1 expression was evaluated via qPCR, ELISA, and flow cytometry, while the functional recruitment γδ T cells recruitment was quantified using transwell migration assays. In vitro, Stx2a significantly upregulates CX3CL1 mRNA and protein secretion in HGEC. In silico profiling of acute kidney injury (AKI) tissues confirmed widespread CX3CL1 upregulation in the damaged parenchyma and identified a distinct TRGV9+ cell cluster expressing CX3CR1 transcripts. Contingency analysis showed that TRGV9+ cells were substantially more likely to express CX3CR1 than other T/NKT cells. Importantly, flow cytometry analysis confirmed that γδ T cells express high levels of CX3CR1 protein. Finally, transwell assays demonstrated that both Stx2a-conditioned HGEC media and recombinant CX3CL1 potently induce γδ T cell migration, an effect that was completely abrogated upon disruption of the chemokine gradient. Together, these findings suggest that CX3CL1 release by Stx2a-stimulated endothelial cells contributes to a chemotactic gradient that may mediate the targeted recruitment of circulating CX3CR1+ TRGV9/TRDV2 cells to the injured kidney.

title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis remodels the multi-tissue transcriptional landscape of the host.
abstract: The gut microbiota exerts a profound influence on host physiology, but its systemic impact on gene expression across diverse tissues remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the transcriptional effects of gut microbiota depletion and restoration in mice across six tissues (colon, jejunum, liver, heart, lung, and kidney) using whole-transcriptome sequencing. We found that the presence of gut microbiota significantly altered the transcriptome, with the most pronounced effects in the colon. Using a linear mixed-effects model, we identified 7365 candidate microbiota-responsive genes. Tissue-specific analysis revealed that these genes were associated with distinct functional pathways, such as immunity in the gut and lung, and metabolism in the liver. Further refinement with LASSO regression pinpointed candidate microbiota‑responsive genes, whose ortholog expression levels were significantly associated with patient survival in corresponding human cancers (e.g., LIHC, LUAD, KIRC). Furthermore, we observed a widespread remodeling of competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks by the gut microbiota. Single-cell data analysis highlighted a potential gut-liver axis interaction, primarily mediated by colonic enterocytes and hepatic cholangiocytes, meanwhile gut microbiota repressed the transcription initiation of Noct in colonic enterocytes, whose expression level was significantly negatively correlated to gut-liver axis interaction. Our findings provide a comprehensive map of the multi-tissue transcriptional landscape shaped by the gut microbiota, which regulate immune response of the gut-liver axis according to inhibit the transcription of Noct, revealing tissue-specific regulatory mechanisms and identifying key genes with potential clinical relevance in cancer.﻿ Video Abstract.

title: Immune microenvironment biomarkers linked to ferroptosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by marked metabolic reprogramming and a highly heterogeneous immune microenvironment. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and has been implicated in ccRCC biology. This study aimed to identify immune-microenvironment-associated hub genes in ccRCC, examine their relationship with ferroptosis-related transcriptional changes, and evaluate their diagnostic and cellular-expression characteristics. Public multi-omics data were analyzed using GSE53757 (72 ccRCC and 72 matched normal kidney tissues), GSE159115 single-cell RNA-sequencing data, and TCGA-KIRC (542 primary tumors and 72 normal kidney tissues). Differential expression, hierarchical co-expression clustering, ferroptosis-gene enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, MCP-counter immune scoring, single-cell localization, ROC analysis, and exploratory survival analysis were performed. In addition, in vitro qRT-PCR experiments were performed for SLC7A11, GPX4, ACSL4, and HMOX1 in RPTEC and 786-O cells and for CCR5, CSF1R, and CD86 in macrophage cultures, with three biological replicates per group, using the complete ΔCt/ΔΔCt/2-ΔΔCt validation workflow. GSE53757 identified 8,650 differentially expressed genes, including significant enrichment of detected FerrDb ferroptosis genes (hypergeometric p = 2.3 × 10-3). CCR5, CSF1R, CD86, CD8A, and LCP2 were significantly upregulated and clustered within the ccRCC-associated M03 immune co-expression module. MCP-counter and single-cell analyses localized these signals predominantly to macrophage and T/NK-cell compartments. TCGA-KIRC independently confirmed significant upregulation and diagnostic discrimination (AUC 0.862-0.948; five-gene panel AUC = 0.932), whereas the panel showed no independent overall-survival association. In vitro qRT-PCR measurements confirmed higher relative expression of SLC7A11, GPX4, ACSL4, and HMOX1 in 786-O than in RPTEC cells, with fold changes of 2.55, 1.58, 1.70, and 2.30, respectively; CCR5, CSF1R, and CD86 were also higher in macrophages exposed to 786-O-conditioned medium than in M0 macrophages. CCR5, CSF1R, CD86, CD8A, and LCP2 are best interpreted as immune-microenvironment-associated hub genes in ccRCC rather than canonical ferroptosis drivers. Their association with ferroptosis is supported at the pathway and co-expression levels, while direct regulation of iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, or the GPX4/SLC7A11 axis is not established by the present analyses. The multi-dataset evidence supports their potential diagnostic and immune-stratification value in ccRCC.
