title: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) mediated gut breast crosstalk in breast cancer: integrative network analysis of molecular signaling, immune infiltration and prognostic biomarkers.
abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy in which metabolic dysregulation, immune remodelling, and complex host microbiota interactions contribute to disease progression and therapeutic response. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including acetate, propionate, and butyrate, may act as important molecular mediators linking the gut microbiome to systemic immune and tumor-associated signalling. However, the molecular networks through which SCFA-mediated signalling may influence breast cancer progression and the tumor immune microenvironment remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying the gut-breast axis by integrating SCFA host interaction networks in breast cancer transcriptomic, prognostic, immune infiltration, and drug gene interaction analyses. The SCFA-host interactome was constructed from the combination of HMDB and PubChem data in a protein-protein interaction network. The identification of hub genes was conducted through topological analysis, followed by validation using TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq data, Kaplan-Meier Survival Analysis, TIMER2.0 immune analysis, and DGIdb repurposing analysis. The findings indicated that the genes STAT3, HIF1A, and IL6 served as key nodes connecting SCFA signalling and cancer formation. Selected SCFAs, such as propionate, have direct experimental evidence of involvement in the modulation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway in breast cancer models, while butyrate has been associated with several breast cancer-related signalling and epigenetic mechanisms. Associations were most strongly identified in acetate which was mainly related to metabolic and immune regulatory pathways. This computational analysis did not give a quantitative ranking of the strength of interaction between SCFA and hub genes. In exploratory survival analysis without multiple-testing correction, increased STAT3 and HIF1A expression was associated with unfavourable relapse-free survival. SCFA-associated immune targets showed positive correlations with CD8+ T-cell infiltration. This study identifies the SCFA-host interactome as an essential regulatory network in breast cancer. Uncovering metabolic and signalling chokepoints such as STAT3 leads to the discovery of new biomarkers for prognosis and drug targets. This highlights the possibility of exploiting the gut-breast axis to increase immune cell penetration.

title: Endothelial IFI16 drives vasculopathy and profibrotic remodeling in systemic sclerosis by activating JAK/STAT signaling.
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is characterized by a prominent type I interferon (IFN-I) signature, yet the upstream drivers that link this signature to fibrosis remain unclear. This study aims to identify Interferon gamma-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) as an endothelial mediator that contributes to vasculopathy and fibrotic remodeling in SSc. Machine-learning screening of public bulk RNA-seq was applied to identify fibrosis-associated IFN-I regulators. IFI16 expression pattern was validated by scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence. Functional and pathway analyses were performed in IFI16-overexpressing endothelial cells. A machine-learning-based analysis of bulk RNA-seq datasets demonstrated that IFI16 is significantly upregulated in SSc skin and ranks among the IFN-I-associated genes positively correlated with more severe skin fibrosis, shorter non-Raynaud disease duration, and elevated extracellular matrix deposition. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed the enrichment of IFI16 in endothelial cells, and the co-localization of IFI16 with vasculature was validated by immunofluorescence. IFI16-high endothelial cells exhibited higher IFN activity and enhanced extracellular matrix remodeling. Stimulation with profibrotic or proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TGF-β and IFN-⍺) upregulated IFI16 expression in endothelial cells. Gain-of-function experiments showed that IFI16 overexpression impaired endothelial proliferation, migration, and tube formation, while driving the transition of endothelial cells towards mesenchymal cells through JAK-STAT signaling. Inhibition of JAK-STAT signaling reversed IFI16-induced endothelial-mesenchymal transition. Collectively, endothelial IFI16 coupled IFN-I signaling to vasculopathy and fibrotic remodeling via JAK-STAT activation, highlighting IFI16 as a promising therapeutic target in SSc vasculopathy and the subsequent fibrosis.

title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq.
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data. Validation on synthetic data with known ground-truth parameters confirms high inference accuracy in low-to-medium activation regimes and shows that recovery of BS and productive BF becomes increasingly condition-dependent as the ON-state probability approaches saturation; under different recovery criteria, the condition-specific upper Pon limit for simultaneously recovering BS and productive BF varies with cell number and capture efficiency. Applied to a mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) dataset, PhysInfer reconstructs a transcriptional dynamic manifold across the 2,137-gene secondary BIC analysis set, showing cross-gene variation in fitted burst frequency and burst size. A model-specific stationary likelihood combined with zero-count anchoring improves robustness to zero-heavy observations. The adaptive topology module further identifies a distinct subset of genes with stable support for an effective sequential 3-state representation, revealing distributional structure beyond that captured by standard 2-state fitting. PhysInfer thus provides a robust, topology-adaptive, and interpretable solution for characterizing transcriptional kinetic patterns from static single-cell transcriptomic snapshots.

title: A SERPINA1-associated SOX4-FN1 epithelial program linked to lymphatic endothelial responses in aggressive papillary thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) complicates risk assessment and treatment planning in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). How tumor epithelial programs relate to the lymphatic microenvironment remains unclear. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data with bulk cohorts to characterize epithelial states and their clinical associations. Bulk cohorts came from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Deconvolution, pathway, regulatory, and cell-cell communication analyses examined epithelial-lymphatic relationships; machine learning was used to construct an LNM classifier. We tested key findings using perturbation and rescue experiments, lymphatic endothelial cell (LEC) assays, xenografts, and human tissue analyses. An atlas of 221,187 cells from 46 thyroid specimens identified an extracellular matrix-associated THY5 epithelial state. THY5 was enriched in pooled cells from aggressive tumors, although its sample-level abundance did not differ significantly between tumor groups. Bulk analyses linked higher estimated THY5 abundance to adverse clinicopathological features and immune exclusion. An exploratory 11-gene classifier incorporating SERPINA1 and FN1 discriminated lymph node status. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.810 in the TCGA internal evaluation set and 0.768 and 0.800 in two GEO cohorts. Communication and spatial analyses implicated FN1-related epithelial-lymphatic interactions and local THY5-LEC co-occurrence. Perturbation experiments supported functional relationships among SERPINA1, SOX4, and FN1. SOX4 re-expression increased FN1 mRNA and protein levels relative to SERPINA1 knockdown alone. FN1 re-expression in SERPINA1-depleted tumor cells counteracted reductions in LEC markers, tube formation, and migration. SERPINA1 knockdown also suppressed xenograft growth and reduced FN1 staining. Our findings support functional links among SERPINA1-associated SOX4-FN1 expression, malignant epithelial behavior and LEC responses in PTC, highlighting the potential of this molecular program for investigating epithelial-lymphatic interactions. The 11-gene LNM classifier discriminated lymph node status across the evaluated cohorts, providing an exploratory framework for molecularly informed risk assessment.

title: Diet-induced obesity disrupts hypothalamic- testicular NF-κB signaling axis and impairs spermatogenesis: an integrated transcriptomic analysis and meta-analysis.
abstract: Obesity is a recognized risk factor for male infertility, yet the involvement of the hypothalamic-testicular axis and nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB)-mediated inflammation remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to investigate whether diet-induced obesity is associated with alterations in the hypothalamic-testicular NF-κB signaling axis and spermatogenesis through integrated transcriptomic analysis and clinical meta-analysis. Testicular single-cell RNA-seq and hypothalamic transcriptomic data from diet-induced obese mice were integrated to identify cell-type-specific transcriptional changes. The analyses included differential expression, pathway enrichment, and NF-κB activity scoring based on target gene expression. Mechanistic findings related to steroidogenesis and germ-cell maturation were elucidated via integrated transcriptomic analysis, and a systematic clinical meta-analysis was further performed to validate these mechanistic insights and assess the association between obesity, sperm quality, and NF-κB-related inflammation in humans. Integrated analysis revealed marked NF-κB transcriptional activity in testicular germ cells (predominantly round spermatids, adjusted p = 0.00134), whose median score was 1.82-fold higher than that of the control group. This activity inversely correlated with genes essential for steroidogenesis (Hsd3b1: r = -0.47 to -0.62), blood-testis barrier (BTB) integrity (Cldn11: r ≈ -0.55), and germ-cell maturation (Tnp1: r = -0.42 to -0.58; all adjusted p < 0.05). Concurrently, a high-fat diet was associated with hypothalamic NF-κB signaling (log2FC = 1.32, adjusted p = 0.012) and upregulated Protein Phosphatase 2 Catalytic Subunit Alpha (Ppp2ca; log2FC = 1.57, adjusted p = 0.008). Meta-analysis of 7 clinical studies confirmed obesity-associated reduced sperm concentration (standardized mean difference = -0.24, 95% CI: -0.37 to -0.12, p < 0.001) and 3.24-fold higher azoospermia risk (95% CI:1.18-8.88, p = 0.023). Collectively, these findings suggest that NF-κB-mediated inflammation along the hypothalamus-testis axis may contribute to obesity-related male infertility and highlight NF-κB as a potential therapeutic target. However, further interventional studies using NF-κB inhibitors or germ cell-specific genetic models are required to establish causality and validate NF-κB as a therapeutic target.

title: A seven-gene signature diagnostic model for early-onset colorectal cancer and the tumor-suppressive role of SLC26A2 via redox modulation.
abstract: The rising incidence and poor prognosis of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) highlight an urgent need for effective diagnostic biomarkers. This study integrates RNA sequencing data with machine learning algorithms to identify EOCRC-specific genes and construct a diagnostic model to improve molecular diagnosis and explore the functional role of key genes. We analyzed RNA sequencing data from EOCRC patients (age ≤ 50) obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between EOCRC and normal tissues were identified and subjected to construct a diagnostic model through random forest analysis and artificial neural network modeling. The diagnostic performance of the model was evaluated in a training set and validated in an independent set. CIBERSORT was utilized to investigate the immune cell infiltration patterns. The expression levels of key DEGs were further verified in 15 paired clinical tissues. Moreover, RT-qPCR and western blotting were applied to detect the expression of solute carrier member 26 family 2 (SLC26A2), which is one of the top-ranked genes, in CRC cell lines. The functional role of SLC26A2 was investigated in EOCRC cell lines (SW480 and HT29) through lentivector-mediated ectopic overexpression experiments assessing proliferation, migration and invasion. The association between SLC26A2 and the cytotoxicity of vanadium-containing compounds (BMOV, VO(acac)₂) was explored, focusing on redox modulation (ROS/GSH levels) using inhibitors (BSO) and antioxidants (NAC). We identified 22 DEGs between EOCRC tumor and normal tissues. A machine learning-based diagnostic model based on seven DEGs (SLC26A2, FCGBP, SLC7A5, CA2, STC2, SLC4A4 and THBS2) for EOCRC was constructed. The model achieved an AUC of 0.987 (training) and 0.874 (validation). Immune profiling revealed altered infiltration of monocytes, M0 macrophages, and γδ T cells in EOCRC. Experimental validation confirmed the dysregulation of the seven key genes. SLC26A2 was downregulated in EOCRC tissues and its overexpression significantly inhibited cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. Transcriptomic analysis linked SLC26A2 overexpression to glutathione (GSH) metabolism. EOCRC cells exhibited sensitivity to vanadium compounds, which was enhanced by SLC26A2 overexpression. SLC26A2 expression correlated with compound-induced cytotoxicity alongside modulation of ROS/GSH levels, as evidenced by the synergistic effect of BSO (GSH inhibitor) and the attenuating effect of NAC (antioxidant). We developed and validated a robust machine learning-based diagnostic model for EOCRC using a 7-gene signature. The downregulated gene SLC26A2 acts as a tumor suppressor in EOCRC and is associated with cellular sensitivity to vanadium-containing compounds, potentially through a redox-dependent mechanism linked to GSH metabolism. These findings provide novel insights into the identification of diagnostic biomarkers and highlight the therapeutic potential for EOCRC.

title: ESRRA facilitates hepatocellular carcinoma progression through transcriptional activation of PHF5A and serves as a potential therapeutic target of rosuvastatin.
abstract: The estrogen-related receptor alpha (ESRRA), a member of the estrogen receptor-related receptor family, has been implicated in tumor progression across multiple cancers. However, its function and molecular mechanisms in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain incompletely understood. Moreover, statins improve the prognosis of HCC patients in clinical trials, while the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. ESRRA expression was analyzed in public databases, clinical HCC tissues and cell lines. The effects of ESRRA and rosuvastatin on HCC cell proliferation and migration were examined in vitro (CCK-8, colony formation, EdU proliferation, wound-healing, transwell assays, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) marker analysis) and in vivo (subcutaneous xenograft, lung metastasis, and orthotopic liver tumor models). RNA sequencing, dual-luciferase reporter assays, ChIP-qPCR, and co-IP identified ESRRA's downstream targets and pathways. ESRRA was significantly upregulated in clinical HCC specimens and cell lines. Functional assays showed that ESRRA promoted HCC cell proliferation and migration in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, ESRRA interacted with coactivator PGC1α and transcriptionally upregulated PHD finger protein 5 A (PHF5A), which was associated with enhanced PI3K/AKT signaling and downstream genes related to cell cycle progression and apoptosis. Furthermore, rosuvastatin exerted anti-tumor activity in HCC and potentiated lenvatinib-induced HCC cell suppression by downregulating ESRRA and inhibiting its transcriptional function via reducing intracellular cholesterol. ESRRA/PGC1α promotes HCC progression via an ESRRA-PHF5A axis that is required for PI3K/AKT pathway activity and mediates rosuvastatin's anti-tumor effect. Targeting ESRRA-PHF5A may be a therapeutic strategy for HCC.

title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) identified a highly malignant EMT epithelial subpopulation characterized by elevated genomic instability and terminal malignant states. Furthermore, an ensemble of machine learning algorithms prioritized C16orf74 as a key EMT-associated malignant regulator. Spatial transcriptomics localized C16orf74 spatially concentrated at invasive-front and transitory regions associated with distinct tumor microenvironmental niches. Gain- and loss-of-function assays confirmed that C16orf74 regulates EMT activation, migration, invasion, and tumor-sphere formation in HNSCC cells. Mechanistically, integrative regulon, transcriptomic, spatial, and functional analyses identified high-mobility group AT-hook 2 (HMGA2) as a candidate downstream mediator of C16orf74-associated EMT. To translate these biological insights into clinical practice, we developed an EMT-based pathomics prognostic model using hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images, which achieved robust prognostic stratification. Notably, high-risk group interpretably exhibited a positive correlation with C16orf74 expression, EMT enrichment, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and resistance to standard chemotherapeutic agents. Collectively, our findings identify C16orf74 as a putative EMT regulator and develop a clinically accessible pathomics model for prognostic and therapeutic stratification in HNSCC.

title: CD39-associated myeloid-T-cell coordination within an immunoregulatory neighborhood linked to treatment resistance in triple-negative breast cancer.
abstract: Immunotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains limited, partly due to mechanisms of immune suppression within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase 1 (ENTPD1, encoding cluster of differentiation 39, CD39) is a key immunoregulatory ectonucleotidase, but its treatment-associated distribution and coordination across myeloid and T-cell states in TNBC remain incompletely characterized. We re-analyzed a single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset comprising 156120 immune cells from 27 tumor and metastatic samples across 14 patients with TNBC. Trajectory and cell-cell communication analyses were complemented by NicheNet, independent single-cell and bulk transcriptomic validation, CosMx spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. CD39 protein expression and its association with survival were evaluated in an independent cohort of 112 patients with TNBC using immunohistochemistry (IHC), Kaplan-Meier analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Three signed-R2-based summary indices-treatment contribution (TC), ENTPD1 dynamic index (EDI), and tumor response index (TRI)-were applied to summarize treatment-associated immune dynamics. ENTPD1 expression was observed across macrophage and regulatory T-cell states, including CD4+CD39+ Tregs. Higher macrophage ENTPD1 expression was associated with M2-related programs, attenuated stimulator of interferon genes (STING)-type I interferon signaling, and reduced antigen-presentation programs. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed preferential interactions between myeloid cells and CD4+CD39+ T cells. Inferred lymphotoxin (LT) signaling involving CD4+CD39+ T cells and myeloid populations was higher in non-responders. Cross-cohort and patient-level analyses supported coordinated CD39-associated immune programs, while spatial transcriptomics and representative multiplex immunofluorescence imaging visualized the implicated populations within shared tumor regions. In the independent IHC cohort, high tissue-level CD39 expression remained independently associated with shorter overall survival (OS) after adjustment for age group and American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) stage. ENTPD1/CD39 was associated with coordinated myeloid and T-cell states, an adenosine-related immunoregulatory context, and reduced response to anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) therapy plus chemotherapy in TNBC. These findings support further evaluation of ENTPD1/CD39-associated immune states in the context of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). High tissue-level CD39 expression was independently associated with shorter OS in an independent clinical cohort.

title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

title: Multi-omics integration identifies serum FTL as a novel diagnostic biomarker for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a common malignant tumor in China, with a poor five-year survival rate due to the lack of effective early diagnostic methods. This study aimed to identify potential non-invasive biomarkers and clarify their underlying mechanisms. We employed an integrative approach combining serum proteomic profiling, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analyses. Quantitative proteomics was conducted on 15 serum samples of treatment-naive early-stage ESCC patients and 5 from healthy controls. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were cross-referenced with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from the GSE53624 dataset, and a diagnostic model was developed using LASSO regression. Cross-validation was performed using scRNA-seq data. The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was utilized to validate FTL in 155 serum samples from two centers. In silico FTL knockouts were conducted using scTenifoldKnk, followed by GO, KEGG, and PPI network analyses. Proteomic profiling identified a total of 129 DEPs. Intersection with GSE53624 DEGs yielded 8 overlapping genes, and a 6-biomarker (TF, CHAD, CSRP1, FCGR3A, RCN1, FTL) diagnostic model was built, with AUC 0.882-1.0 across validation cohorts. scRNA-seq intersection analysis identified FTL as the only overlapping DEG, exhibiting high expression levels in ESCC epithelial cells and macrophages. FTL demonstrated strong standalone diagnostic performance, with AUC values ranging from 0.872 to 0.970 across three GEO datasets. ELISA validation yielded an AUC of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.674-0.816) and 0.838 (95% CI: 0.751-0.905) for early-stage ESCC, surpassing the performance of CEA and SCCA. The combination of FTL with SCCA further enhanced discriminatory efficacy. Mechanistically, FTL was associated with altered immune cell infiltration, characterized by increased resting dendritic cells and M2 macrophages and decreased follicular helper T cells, as well as activation of the ferroptosis pathway. In silico FTL knockouts revealed DEGs enriched in stress and metabolic biological processes, extracellular vesicles (cellular component), transcriptional regulation (molecular function, CHOP-ATF3 complex), IL-17/TNF pathways, and lipid/ROS-related pathways. Protein-protein interaction hubs included FOS, ATF3, NFKBIA, and CXCL8, with FTL linked to NFE2L2, TFRC, and TXNRD1. FTL represents a credible non-invasive serum diagnostic biomarker for ESCC. Computational analyses suggest it is a candidate molecule requiring further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

title: Mechanistic insights and translational perspectives on liver fibrosis through single-cell transcriptomics.
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a defining feature of chronic liver diseases and can progress to cirrhosis and liver failure. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution analysis of cellular heterogeneity and multicellular interactions during fibrogenesis. In this narrative review, we analyzed published single-cell transcriptomic studies from experimental models and human cohorts, focusing on cell-type-specific programs, cell-state trajectories inferred by Monocle, and intercellular communication networks predicted using CellChat and CellPhoneDB. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) consistently emerged as the primary extracellular matrix-producing cells, with conserved activation signatures involving collagen synthesis, Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-Protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) signaling, and matrix organization. Macrophage analyses identified fibrosis-associated subsets, including CD9+ and TREM2+ scar-associated macrophages (SAMs), which regulate inflammation, angiogenesis, and stromal remodeling. Liver sinusoidal endothelial cells undergo capillarization and transcriptional reprogramming linked to WNT signaling and antigen presentation. B cells exhibit activation signatures related to B-cell receptor signaling. Trajectory analyses infer potential cell-state transitions based on transcriptional similarity from quiescent to pathogenic states, including stepwise HSC activation and monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation. Cell-cell communication analysis highlights HSC-macrophage interactions, with key axes such as predicted Chemokine ligand 2-chemokine receptor 2 (CCL2-CCR2) and transforming growth factor-β-transforming growth factor-β receptor (TGFβ-TGFβR) signaling interactions that may contribute to fibrogenic communication networks. These findings define conserved multicellular programs and support integrated multi-omics approaches for biomarker discovery and therapy.

title: Comprehensive Immunoprofiling and Multi-Omics Modeling Reveal Key Immune Features Associated with Disease Progression and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Comprehensive profiling of peripheral immune cells has shown prognostic and disease-monitoring value across multiple cancers, but its clinical relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly unresectable HCC, remains insufficiently defined. To address this gap, we performed integrated peripheral immunoprofiling combining T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing, flow cytometry-based T-cell phenotyping, bulk RNA sequencing, and public single-cell RNA-seq analysis in healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients. This design enabled characterization of HCC-associated and stage-associated peripheral immune alterations and identification of immunotherapy-relevant features in unresectable HCC. Single-cell analysis and flow cytometry revealed remodeling of circulating T-cell states in unresectable HCC, including reduced naïve-like compartments, enrichment of Treg-like cells, and increased memory/effector differentiation. TCR repertoire analysis showed reduced diversity, increased clonal dominance, altered V-J gene usage, decreased interindividual sharing, and convergent motif-level alterations, with early CD4+ TCR perturbations in resectable HCC and more pronounced CD8+ repertoire restriction in unresectable disease. Exploratory GLIPH-based motif analysis, HLA inference, and peptide-HLA binding prediction suggested candidate motif-HLA antigen associations involving hepatitis virus-derived antigens and recurrent HCC mutation-derived candidate neoantigens, although experimental validation is required. Bulk RNA-seq of peripheral CD8+ T cells revealed higher Activation/Effector function, Exhaustion, and Anergy signature scores in both resectable and unresectable HCC than in HDs, with no significant differences between the two HCC groups, whereas the Chemokine/Chemokine receptor signature was specifically increased in unresectable HCC. The overall IFN-response signature did not differ significantly among the three groups. Integrative machine-learning models were then developed using 818 peripheral immune-related features. Among them, the random forest (RF) model effectively distinguished healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients, with consistently high sensitivity and area under the curve (AUC) in both cross-validation and an independent validation cohort. In unresectable HCC patients receiving immunotherapy, four features derived from TCR-seq and T-cell subset profiling discriminated responders (CR/PR) from non-responders (SD/PD) in univariate analyses, while multivariate prioritization further highlighted ULBP1 as a consistently prioritized response-associated feature that requires validation in an independent cohort. Overall, this study supports comprehensive peripheral immune profiling as an exploratory framework for identifying stage-associated immune alterations and candidate biomarkers to inform personalized immunotherapy strategies in HCC.

title: White Blood Cell Count-related Biomarkers for Acute Myocardial Infarction: Integrative Analysis of Mouse Models and Clinical Samples.
abstract: Although white blood cell count (WBC) is an accessible prognostic marker, the relationship between WBC-related genes and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. A retrospective study of 1,917 patients with AMI was conducted to estimate prognostic indicators. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was used to identify potential genes associated with the prognostic indicators, and the resulting genes were intersected with differentially expressed genes from the key monocyte subset identified in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyses. Key genes were screened by integrating 52 machine learning algorithms. The expression of key genes was validated by RT-qPCR with clinical samples. In addition, an AMI mouse model was established, and the expression of related proteins was further validated by western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Age, WBC, and serum potassium (K) level were identified as prognostic indicators for AMI. Eight key genes were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that these genes were significantly enriched in immune- and inflammation-related pathways. RT-qPCR validation showed that the expression trends of five key genes (ITGA4, RASA3, ATG7, HSPA6, and ITGAM) were consistent with the bioinformatics results, whereas DSTN, FES, and MCL1 did not reach statistical significance. Additionally, WB and IHC further validated HSP70 family protein upregulation in the AMI mouse model. Eight AMI-related genes were identified and might contribute to disease progression through inflammatory regulation. The integration of multi-omics analysis and experimental validation underscores the translational potential of these genes. Although further experimental validation is warranted, these findings may offer novel insights for the development of therapeutic strategies for AMI. This study identified eight key WBC-related genes that may serve as potential biomarkers for AMI.

title: Keratin 17 drives endometrial cancer aggressiveness via epithelial-mesenchymal transition: a single-cell transcriptomic and integrative bioinformatics study.
abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is a common gynecological malignancy with increasing incidence, and advanced or recurrent cases have limited treatment options. The role of Keratin 17 (KRT17), a type I intermediate filament protein implicated in tumor progression in other cancers, remains unclear in EC. This study aimed to investigate the expression, prognostic significance, and functional mechanisms of KRT17 in EC. Bioinformatics analysis revealed significant upregulation of KRT17 in EC tissues, with elevated expression strongly correlated with adverse clinical outcomes and reduced overall survival. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis elucidated the distribution and expression profiles of KRT17 in malignant epithelial cells of endometrial cancer, and differential expression analysis combined with pathway enrichment analyses further confirmed the significant enrichment of KRT17 in the EMT pathway. In vitro functional assays confirmed that stable knockdown of KRT17 significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, invasion, and spheroid formation of EC cells, and altered the expression of key EMT markers. In vivo animal models demonstrated that KRT17 knockdown effectively suppressed tumor growth and reversed the EMT process. KRT17 is markedly overexpressed in EC, with high levels correlating closely with adverse patient prognosis. Its expression is strongly linked to EMT pathway activation, and KRT17 knockdown not only potently inhibits EC cell proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro, but also blunts tumor progression and reverses EMT in vivo. KRT17 is closely associated with EMT phenotypes in EC, facilitates tumor progression, and correlates with poor clinical prognosis of patients.

title: Analyzing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC): an integrative transcriptomic and computational study.
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), are persistent environmental contaminants. Epidemiological studies have associated PFAS exposure with several cancers, but TNBC-specific molecular evidence remains limited. We integrated computational target prediction, network analysis, bulk transcriptomic and microarray cohorts, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, prognostic modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and expression assessment in 15 paired TNBC and adjacent tissues. The public patient cohorts and tissue specimens did not contain measured PFAS exposure, so all PFAS-related interpretations were prespecified as associative and hypothesis-generating. Results The intersection of 654 predicted PFAS targets, 3,944 TNBC-associated genes, and 27,529 TNBC differentially expressed genes yielded 197 candidates. A hypergeometric test indicated that this overlap exceeded chance expectation (observed/expected = 3.22, P = 3.65 × 10 - 52), although the permissive DEG set and heterogeneous disease-gene sources remain important limitations. Six candidate genes (CDK9, PF4, VEGFC, FABP7, NR2F6, and PLAU) formed the prognostic signature. The 2-year training-set AUC of 0.999 was interpreted as probable optimism rather than clinical-level performance. RT-qPCR showed significant differences for CDK9, PF4, VEGFC, FABP7, and NR2F6, whereas PLAU was directionally increased but not significant. Docking and simulation supported computational compatibility for selected protein-PFAS complexes but did not demonstrate cellular target engagement. The findings define a TNBC gene signature that overlaps with predicted PFAS targets and provide a testable computational hypothesis. Causal inference requires PFAS-stratified patient cohorts, direct exposure transcriptomics, dose-response experiments, and independent prospective validation.
